raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With a hybrid SWA KV pool, the torch_native backend writes a sliding-window layer's K/V at SWA-pool ids (`swa_out_cache_loc`), but reads it back with the full-pool ids in `req_to_token`. The SWA sub-pool numbers its slots on its own, so once the two id spaces drift apart the reads gather other tokens' rows, and once a full id passes the SWA pool's size the gather raises `IndexError` and the forward crashes.

intel_amx had the same problem and got `_swa_kv_indices` in #44666, but torch_native wasn't changed. It's the default backend on Apple MPS, arm64 CPU hosts and HPU, and `_hybrid_swa_memory_backend_disable` only drops the SWA pool for aiter, wave and flex_attention, so hybrid-SWA models like Gemma 3 and Gemma 4 hit this there.

## Modifications

- `torch_native_backend.py`: add `_kv_indices`, which for a layer routed to the SWA sub-pool translates this batch's `req_to_token` rows to SWA ids once per forward (the same thing intel_amx does) and returns that table with `arange` row indices. Full-attention and cross-attention layers keep reading `req_to_token` as before. `forward_extend` and `forward_decode` pass its result to the SDPA loops, which don't change.
- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_torch_native_swa_pool_reads.py` (base-a-test-cpu). It builds a real `SWAKVPool`, `SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` and `RunnerIds`, makes the full and SWA ids diverge the way eviction does, runs extend then decode on a sliding-window layer, and checks the output against SDPA over the raw q/k/v with the window mask. One subtest keeps the full ids inside the SWA buffer (wrong rows), the other lets them run past it (`IndexError`). A full-attention layer is checked too.

## Accuracy Tests

On main the new test fails with every element mismatched in the first subtest and `IndexError: index 25 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 25` in the second. With this change both pass. Layers that don't live in the SWA sub-pool read exactly what they read before. I haven't run a model end to end on MPS or an arm64 host.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Only SWA-routed layers on a hybrid pool pay anything: one gather over the batch's rows per forward, shared by every sliding-window layer.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation. Not needed.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. See above, CPU unit test only.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

I drafted this change with an AI assistant, then reviewed and tested it myself.

+"""torch_native reads a sliding-window layer's KV at the slots it wrote.
+
+With a hybrid SWA pool, a sliding-window layer's K/V lives in the SWA sub-pool,
+which numbers its slots apart from the full pool. The backend writes there at
+the translated ``swa_out_cache_loc``; its reads must translate the full-pool ids
+in ``req_to_token`` the same way, or they gather other tokens' rows, and once a
+full id passes the SWA pool's size they index past its buffer.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+from sglang.test.test_utils import maybe_stub_sgl_kernel
+
+maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.torch_native_backend import TorchNativeAttnBackend
+from sglang.srt.layers.radix_attention import RadixAttention
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.swa import SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.kv.alloc.runner_ids import RunnerIds
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.memory_pool import ReqToTokenPool
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.swa_memory_pool import SWAKVPool
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_batch_info import ForwardMode
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+HEADS, HEAD_DIM, WINDOW = 2, 8, 3
+SWA_LAYER, FULL_LAYER = 0, 1
+
+
+class TestTorchNativeSWAPoolReads(CustomTestCase):
+    def _build(self, size, size_swa):
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        self.pool = SWAKVPool(
+            size=size,
+            size_swa=size_swa,
+            page_size=1,
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+            head_num=HEADS,
+            head_dim=HEAD_DIM,
+            swa_attention_layer_ids=[SWA_LAYER],
+            full_attention_layer_ids=[FULL_LAYER],
+            device="cpu",
+        )
+        self.allocator = SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator(
+            size=size,
+            size_swa=size_swa,
+            page_size=1,
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+            device="cpu",
+            kvcache=self.pool,
+            need_sort=True,
+        )
+        self.req_to_token_pool = ReqToTokenPool(
+            size=2, max_context_len=32, device="cpu", enable_memory_saver=False
+        )
+        runner_ids = RunnerIds(
+            req_to_token=self.req_to_token_pool.req_to_token,
+            token_to_kv_pool_allocator=self.allocator,
+            token_to_kv_pool=self.pool,
+            page_size=1,
+            device="cpu",
+        )
+        self.backend = TorchNativeAttnBackend(
+            SimpleNamespace(
+                device="cpu",
+                req_to_token_pool=self.req_to_token_pool,
+                token_to_kv_pool=self.pool,
+                runner_ids=runner_ids,
+            )
+        )
+
+    def _layer(self, layer_id, window):
+        return RadixAttention(
+            num_heads=HEADS,
+            head_dim=HEAD_DIM,
+            scaling=HEAD_DIM**-0.5,
+            num_kv_heads=HEADS,
+            layer_id=layer_id,
+            sliding_window_size=window,
+        )
+
+    def _diverged_slots(self, num_tokens):
+        # One request's out-of-window SWA slots are evicted, another request
+        # finishes: the next request's full ids and SWA ids now disagree.
+        evicted = self.allocator.alloc(12)
+        finished = self.allocator.alloc(12)
+        self.allocator.free_swa(evicted)
+        self.allocator.free(finished)
+        full = self.allocator.alloc(num_tokens)
+        swa = self.allocator.translate_loc_from_full_to_swa(full)
+        self.assertFalse(torch.equal(full, swa))
+        return full
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _reference(q, k, v, window):
+        # q: [q_len, H, D] at the last q_len positions of k/v: [kv_len, H, D].
+        q_len, kv_len = q.shape[0], k.shape[0]
+        q_pos = torch.arange(kv_len - q_len, kv_len).unsqueeze(1)
+        k_pos = torch.arange(kv_len).unsqueeze(0)
+        mask = k_pos <= q_pos
+        if window > -1:
+            mask &= k_pos >= q_pos - window
+        return torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(
+            q.transpose(0, 1),
+            k.transpose(0, 1),
+            v.transpose(0, 1),
+            attn_mask=mask,
+            scale=HEAD_DIM**-0.5,
+        ).transpose(0, 1)
+
+    def _check(self, layer_id, window):
+        layer = self._layer(layer_id, window)
+        prompt_len = 7
+        slots = self._diverged_slots(prompt_len + 1)
+        self.req_to_token_pool.req_to_token[0, : prompt_len + 1] = slots
+        q, k, v = (
+            torch.randn(prompt_len + 1, HEADS, HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.float32)
+            for _ in range(3)
+        )
+
+        extend_batch = SimpleNamespace(
+            forward_mode=ForwardMode.EXTEND,
+            out_cache_loc=slots[:prompt_len],
+            req_pool_indices=torch.tensor([0]),
+            seq_lens=torch.tensor([prompt_len]),
+            extend_prefix_lens=torch.tensor([0]),
+            extend_seq_lens=torch.tensor([prompt_len]),
+            encoder_lens=None,
+        )
+        self.backend.init_forward_metadata(extend_batch)
+        out = self.backend.forward_extend(
+            q[:prompt_len].flatten(1),
+            k[:prompt_len],
+            v[:prompt_len],
+            layer,
+            extend_batch,
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            out.view(prompt_len, HEADS, HEAD_DIM),
+            self._reference(q[:prompt_len], k[:prompt_len], v[:prompt_len], window),
+        )
+
+        decode_batch = SimpleNamespace(
+            forward_mode=ForwardMode.DECODE,
+            out_cache_loc=slots[prompt_len:],
+            req_pool_indices=torch.tensor([0]),
+            seq_lens=torch.tensor([prompt_len + 1]),
+            encoder_lens=None,
+        )
+        self.backend.init_forward_metadata(decode_batch)
+        out = self.backend.forward_decode(
+            q[prompt_len:].flatten(1),
+            k[prompt_len:],
+            v[prompt_len:],
+            layer,
+            decode_batch,
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            out.view(1, HEADS, HEAD_DIM), self._reference(q[prompt_len:], k, v, window)
+        )
+
+    def test_sliding_window_layer_reads_its_own_slots(self):
+        # Equal pools: the full ids stay inside the SWA buffer but name other
+        # rows. A larger full pool: they also run past the SWA buffer's end.
+        for size in (24, 64):
+            with self.subTest(full_pool_size=size):
+                self._build(size=size, size_swa=24)
+                self._check(SWA_LAYER, WINDOW)
+
+    def test_full_layer_reads_full_slots(self):
+        self._build(size=64, size_swa=24)
+        self._check(FULL_LAYER, -1)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
